test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. If the length of each train is 350 m and they cross each other in 14 seconds, then what is the speed of each train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite direction ⇒ relative speed = sum of speeds

Total distance = 350 + 350 = 700 m

Relative speed = 700 ÷ 14 = 50 m/s

Each train speed = 50 ÷ 2

**∴ Answer = 25 m/s**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of each train = 350 m

Time = 14 seconds

Opposite direction

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 350 + 350 = 700 m

⇒ Relative speed = 700 ÷ 14 = 50 m/s

⇒ Let speed of each train = v

⇒ Opposite direction ⇒ relative speed = 2v

⇒ 2v = 50

⇒ v = 25 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 25 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Opposite direction ⇒ speeds are added

Train Crossing Concept

Total distance = sum of both train lengths

Speed Formula

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Equal Speed Case

If both speeds are same, each = (relative speed ÷ 2)
